display.purpose: Page headline. The hero raises the ceiling to clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 4.05rem). Always text-wrap: balance.

headline.purpose: Section headings and every kit-finder question. One question per screen means the question is the headline.

slab.purpose: The claim at the top of a moss or pale slab, held to a 20ch measure so it breaks into short lines.

amount.purpose: Prices and kit totals. Tightest tracking in the system; the unit rides alongside at 14px in ink-3.

title.purpose: Card headings, kit line names, step titles. 18px at -0.02em.

lede.purpose: The ink-2 sentence under every headline. Max 56ch, 46ch in the hero. Never longer than two sentences.

label.purpose: Uppercase meta above or beneath a value - ONE PER BEDSIDE, ACTIVE TODAY, OF USUAL, AT HOME, EXAMPLE READING. 10.5-13px at +0.02em to +0.14em.

displayHero.purpose: The landing page's opening headline only. clamp(2.5rem, 6vw, 4.05rem).

amountSmall.purpose: The kit total on the summary. 34px, tightest tracking.

heading.purpose: Slab and card headings inside a panel. 24px.

supporting.purpose: The main reading inside a card or slab: item descriptions, privacy paragraph, explainer body. 16px.

caption.purpose: Secondary meta: room labels, skip lines, left-out lines, gallery captions, legend pills. 14px.

shadows.name: dial-float
shadows.purpose: Under the room-activity dial, the largest circular data object, so it hovers over the page ground.

shadows.name: medallion-lift
shadows.purpose: Under a circular photograph overlapping a slab edge; paired with a 7px ground-coloured ring.

shadows.name: live-halo
shadows.purpose: Around the 8px lime dot meaning a room is in use now.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Around a focused input or select on pale ground, alongside an ink-2 border. The kit finder uses .45.

shadows.name: focus-halo-on-moss
shadows.purpose: The same focus halo inside a moss slab, where the border also goes lime.

shadows.name: now-halo
shadows.purpose: Around the current progress segment in the kit finder.

shadows.name: completion-halo
shadows.purpose: Around the lime tick on the reserved state. The largest halo in the system, used once, at the end.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The world's one authored motion: 22px rise into place, exponential ease-out, IntersectionObserver-driven at rootMargin 0 0 -8% 0 and threshold .06.

motion.name: settle-stagger
motion.purpose: Transition delay across a group of settling elements, cycling every four.

motion.name: settle-failsafe
motion.purpose: Timeout that reveals every settle target and disconnects the observer, so content can never be stranded invisible.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: The kit finder's per-step entrance: 16px travel on the same curve.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, background and border transitions on buttons, inputs, choices and kit lines.

motion.name: tap
motion.purpose: The primary button's 1px active nudge and a checkmark's opacity.

motion.name: progress
motion.purpose: Progress segment background and halo as the flow advances.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables settle, rise, and the progress transition entirely
motion.purpose: Non-negotiable. Reveals degrade to plain visible content.

narrative.overview:
WavePresence is care technology that has to disappear into somebody's mother's kitchen. The world is built from two halves that argue with each other and settle: real photographs of living, ordinary objects - a succulent in a concrete planter, a stone on a nightstand - carry the organic half, and dark glass pills, acid-lime rings and tight geometric type float on top of them as the tech half. Neither half is decoration. The photograph is the product; the glass and the lime are the reading.

The ground is a pale mint (#F1F5EE), never white, and it is the default state of every page. Depth arrives only twice, and only under circles. Colour is rationed hard: deep moss is a slab you use when a passage must stop the scroll, and acid lime is a single signal that means this is live or this is chosen - never a price, never body text, never a link. Everything else is a green-black ink ramp on pale mint, with hairlines instead of boxes wherever a hairline will do.

This refuses two defaults at once. It refuses the eldercare category - white clinical panels, blue "medical alert" chrome, stock photos of smiling seniors - and it equally refuses the warm-parchment wellness page this site used to be. The buyer is fifty to seventy, on a phone, usually in daylight, deciding whether to spend money on their parent's safety. Light ground, large targets, plain sentences, and one loud colour used sparingly enough that it still means something when it appears.
keyCharacteristics: Pale mint ground, never white; paper white is a card, not a page.
One acid-lime signal, meaning live or chosen, and nothing else.
Deep moss slabs, rationed to the passage that must stop the scroll.
Manrope 800 at negative tracking for everything structural; nothing decorative.
Photographs of real objects, with dark glass floating on top of them.
Circles are the data form: rings, arcs, dials, medallions, pucks.
Hairlines, not boxes. Nearly everything is flat.
One authored motion: content settles like a reading landing.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Lime means live or chosen. If a lime mark on screen does not answer "what is happening right now" or "what did I pick", it is wrong. Prices, links, body text and headings are never lime.

rules.name: The Rationed Moss Rule
rules.body: A moss slab is a scroll-stopper, so a page gets at most a couple. On the landing page it is the privacy claim and the Care card. Adding a third moss block does not make the page richer; it makes the first two stop working.

rules.name: The Lime-Inside-Moss Rule
rules.body: Moss is the only surface where lime may act as an accent rather than a signal: the emphasised word in a slab headline, the shield icon in the privacy pill, and the huge rgba(195,245,60,.12) ring bleeding off the slab's corner. Outside moss, that licence is revoked.

rules.name: The Dimmed Hairline Rule
rules.body: A lime hairline is always a tint, never full strength: rgba(195,245,60,.3) on moss, rgba(195,245,60,.45) on pale. A full-strength lime rule would outshine the one mark on the page that means live.

rules.name: The Tighter-Bigger Rule
rules.body: Tracking is a function of size and runs the whole ramp: display -0.045em, amounts -0.055em, titles -0.015em to -0.035em, body normal, labels positive from +0.02em up to +0.14em. Nothing in this world is set at default tracking and large.

rules.name: The Emphasis-Is-Lighter Rule
rules.body: Emphasis inside a headline is <em> rendered as upright and quieter, never italic and never bolder: ink-3 on pale ground, lime on moss. "Monitoring a loved one's safety without being intrusive" reads with its pivot word dropping back, not leaping forward.

rules.name: The 800-Or-400 Rule
rules.body: Structure is 800; prose is 400; 600-700 exists only for small interface text (labels, chips, notes). There is no 500-weight heading and no 600-weight display.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Every layout resolves to one centred column on a phone. The buyer is on a phone, often at night; there is no horizontal scroll, no carousel, and no two-up that survives below 560px.

rules.name: The Content Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: Add a breakpoint at the width where a component actually breaks, and name it for that component. Do not add device-named tiers.

rules.name: The Only Circles Lift Rule
rules.body: A drop shadow is licensed only for a circular object that overlaps something else. Rectangles - cards, slabs, kit lines, inputs - are flat and stay flat; if a rectangle needs separation, change its tone or give it a hairline.

rules.name: The Halo-Not-Glow Rule
rules.body: Every lime box-shadow is spread-only with zero blur. It is a ring, and it means state (live, focused, current, done). Never use a blurred lime glow.

rules.name: The Circle-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Any reading - time of day, share of usual, live/not-live, selected/not - is a circle or an arc. Bars, sparklines and pie wedges have no place in this world. The room-activity dial is the canonical form and the Flutter dashboard inherits it directly.

rules.name: The Dashed-Means-Optional Rule
rules.body: A dashed 1.5px border means the thing is available and not currently chosen. Never use dashed as decoration or as a disabled style.

rules.name: The Never-Stranded Rule
rules.body: Any reveal must degrade to visible: no JS, no observer, reduced motion, or a slow browser all end with the content on screen. A reveal that can hide content permanently is worse than no reveal.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The system has one authored curve, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), and one gesture - settling downward into place. Everything else is a short linear-ish ease on a colour. No bounce, no spring, no parallax, no scroll-jacking.

dos: Do start every surface on pale mint (#F1F5EE) and treat paper white as a raised object on it.
Do spend lime on exactly one thing per screen - the live reading, the chosen item, or the primary action.
Do dim lime to rgba(195,245,60,.12-.45) whenever it is structure (hairlines, slab rings, halos) rather than signal.
Do use a moss slab when a passage must stop the scroll, and let it be rare.
Do draw readings as rings and arcs, with stroke-linecap: round and midnight at the top.
Do set structural type in Manrope 800 with negative tracking, and let emphasis be quieter (ink-3, or lime on moss), never italic.
Do give every interactive element the same 3px lime focus outline at 2px offset.
Do use a 1.5px dashed border for "available, not chosen" and a lime-wash field for "chosen".
Do label demonstration data on the surface that shows it (EXAMPLE READING, Example day).
Do enforce measure - 56ch ledes, 42ch item copy, 20ch slab headlines - so nothing runs as a wall.
Do hold 48px touch targets on steppers and 44px+ on buttons; the buyer is 50-70 and on a phone.
Do re-declare every inherited text role when creating a pale variant of a moss component.
donts: Don't put lime on a price, a heading, body copy, or a link.
Don't add a third moss slab to a page; scarcity is what makes moss work.
Don't use a full-strength lime hairline or a blurred lime glow - tinted rules and spread-only halos only.
Don't put a drop shadow on a rectangle. Separate with tone or a hairline instead.
Don't introduce a second typeface, a serif, or a 500-weight heading.
Don't use italics for emphasis anywhere; <em> is upright and quieter by design.
Don't use the platform's select chevron, checkbox or radio - this world ships its own.
Don't chart with bars, wedges or sparklines; the data form is the ring.
Don't use dark glass anywhere except directly on top of a photograph.
Don't ship a reveal or entrance without a visible fallback under no-JS and prefers-reduced-motion.
Don't add device-named breakpoints; add one where a component actually breaks.
Don't reach for white (#FFFFFF) as a page background.
